serviceModel: Statute allows SEND provision outside Gibraltar, in a Government school, the home or hospital
Parents said they feel they have to go to Spain to see private therapists (2024 review)
Family-focused therapy programmes are shaped to the needs of the child by the paediatric service
A 2024 review weighs spreading LSAs through mainstream classes against SEN in separate settings
terminology: Speech and language difficulties is the SEN category used in Gibraltar school data
The 2024 review records that specific definitions of each type of need are not available
In statute SEND is defined as Supported Educational Needs and Disabilities, not Special
The paediatric service names specific language impairment among the difficulties it supports

sources.label: Laws of Gibraltar, Education and Training Act 1974-11, consolidated to 23 December 2024, ss. 2, 45
HM Government of Gibraltar, Review of factors linked to increased prevalence of special educational needs among children in Gibraltar, 14 March 2024
Supported Needs and Disability Office, Speech and Language Therapy, reproducing the Gibraltar Health Authority service description

serviceModel: Children are seen from birth to 18 in clinic, home, nursery and school
Manx Care's Children's Therapy team delivers it alongside physiotherapy and occupational therapy
Therapists work with off-island specialists as well as health and education colleagues
The service also trains families and the adults who support the child, not only the child
terminology: Developmental Language Disorder is a named specialism within the children's therapy team
The service's remit is difficulties with communication or with eating, drinking and swallowing
The Education Act 2001 fixes only learning difficulty and names no speech or language category
The 2004 SEN Regulations likewise name only learning difficulty, no speech or language category
workforce: The service page says it currently has 10 therapists and 1 assistant, with no date given
Most of the team work part-time, which the page states without giving hours
Therapists are RCSLT members registered with the Health Care Professions Council
The team travels round the island to the child rather than working from its base alone
funding: DHSC must lay an annual Mandate to Manx Care before Tynwald ahead of the financial year
The Mandate sets out the services, funding, performance requirements and objectives
Children's physio, occupational and speech and language therapy is a service named in it
The Mandate must also cover when charges may be made, under Schedule 2 of the 2021 Act

history.description: Education Act 2001 puts the Department under a duty to identify children with special educational needs
Education (Special Educational Needs) Regulations 2004 set the assessment procedure and a parental right of appeal
Manx Care Act 2021 establishes Manx Care as the Statutory Board providing health and care services

Manx Care Act 2021 (AT 2 of 2021), section 12 and Schedule 2
GD 2026/0023, Department of Health and Social Care Mandate to Manx Care 2026/27

workforce: Speech and language therapist is a registrable occupation with a prescribed qualification
The prescribed qualification is entry as a speech and language therapist on the register
That register is the one kept under the Health Professions Order 2001 of the United Kingdom

sources.label: Health Care (Registration) (Prescribed Qualifications) (Jersey) Order 2003, R&O.65/2003, official consolidated version

history.description: The Fondo Assistenza Sanitaria is instituted by Rescritto d'Udienza of 25 July 1953, amended by a rescript of 7 November 1994
The Law on the Government of Vatican City State of 16 July 2002 defines the purposes and territorial competences of the health directorate
Pope Francis approves a new Statute and Regolamento of the Fondo Assistenza Sanitaria by Rescritto d'Udienza of 18 October 2016, in force from 1 February 2017
A new Regolamento of the Direzione di Sanita e Igiene takes effect on 1 March 2022
Article 3 of the F.A.S. Regolamento is amended by rescript of 1 August 2025, governing enrolment of an assisted person's family members

history.description: Article 68 of the 1972 finance law puts the cost of health care in the territory on the State
An ordonnance of 13 January 2000 creates the Agence de sante, charged with drawing up the territory's health programme and with dispensing medicines

history.description: A Special Educational Needs unit is established in the Ministry of Education
A school for learners with hearing impairments, now the Wangsel Institute, is established
The National Policy on Special Educational Needs demands mainstreaming of children with mild to moderate disabilities
The Bhutan Education Blueprint 2014-2024 addresses education for children with disabilities, with the emphasis on expanding special education
Standards for Inclusive Education are established, operationalising inclusion at school level
The National Policy for Persons with Disabilities defines disability on the social model

sources.label: UNICEF ROSA, Mapping of Disability-Inclusive Education Practices in South Asia (2021), country profile: Bhutan — 'Milestones in disability-inclusive education' and Table 1 (Internet Archive copy)

history.description: The Maldives ratifies the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
The Protection of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and Provision of Financial Assistance Act 08/2010, the Disability Act, is enacted
Regulation 2011/R-3 is made under the Disability Act to govern protection of rights and financial assistance
An Inclusive Education Policy is formulated for the first time
Education Act 24/2020 prohibits any form of discrimination against persons with disabilities
The Inclusive Education Policy is revised, repositioning it from special needs to inclusive education
Regulation 2021/R-54 sets the criteria for determining and registering a person as disabled

sources.label: United Nations Maldives, Situational Analysis of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in the Maldives — country report, sections on legislation, registration and inclusive education

history.description: The Ministry of Education establishes an Administration of Special Education
Article 56 of Education Law 1389 obliges the ministry to offer special education and care for disabled students
King Saud University opens the country's first undergraduate programme in speech-language pathology
The Disability Code is enacted, guaranteeing access to free and appropriate educational and rehabilitation services
Article 8 of the Disability Code calls for the creation of a Supreme Council for Disabled Affairs
Regulations of Special Education Programs and Institutes (RSEPI) introduced, reported as the first regulations for students with disabilities
Procedural regulations are issued to organise the institutes and programmes offering special education in the ministry
The Saudi Society of Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology is established

sources.label: UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Saudi Arabia: Inclusion — sections 'Laws, Plans, Policies and Programmes' and 'Governance'
Alakeel, A. I., 'The Practice of Speech-Language Pathology in Saudi Arabia', Arab Journal of Applied Linguistics 7(1), 2022, pp. 87-99 (ERIC full text EJ1375033)

history.description: The Ministry of Education establishes a unit dedicated to inclusion in education
Law No. 34 of 2004 art. 9(1) obliges the state to give full care for the education of children with disabilities
Ministerial Decree No. 515 presses for integration of students with special needs in public schools
The National Plan for Disability 2008-25 makes integrating children with disabilities in schools a priority
Legislative Decree No. 12 of 10 February ratifies the CRPD and its Optional Protocol
Law No. 7 of 2012 art. 2(d) refers students with severe disability to the Ministry of Social Affairs
The Ministry of Health opens four newborn clinics in three governorates for early identification of disabilities

sources.label: UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Syrian Arab Republic: Inclusion — sections 'School Organization', 'Integration', 'Disability' and 'Governance'

history.description: Diagnosis and correction of communication disorders begins as a hospital service at Ramathibodi Hospital
Master's courses are opened in audiology and in speech-language pathology
The Thai Speech-Language and Hearing Association is formally registered on 6 October
National Education Act B.E. 2542 gives persons with communication deficiencies a right to specially provided basic education
Practitioners are required to sit a registration examination for a licence as practitioners of the healing arts
Persons with Disabilities Empowerment Act B.E. 2550 revokes the Act on Rehabilitation of Persons with Disabilities B.E. 2534
The same Act counts impairment in communication among the impairments that make a person disabled
Education Provision for Persons with Disabilities Act B.E. 2551 gives a right to education without cost from birth or from discovery of the disability
The same Act creates a fund for the promotion and development of education for persons with disabilities

funding: The Ministry of Health scheme of charges prices speech therapy, revised from 1 July 2025
Speech therapy is charged at $10.00 per session under Schedule M of that scheme
Children under 12 keep their exemption from charges (MoH scheme of charges FAQ, 2025)
Green and foreign-national Purple IC holders now pay in full for all health services
workforce: Registration needs a basic qualification the AHPCBD recognises and a job offer in Brunei
The newly qualified take conditional registration: a year's supervised practice at minimum
Proof of proficiency in English and in Malay may also be required, where applicable

funding: The State budget funds preschool institutions and those meeting state educational standards
Funding standards are set per student for each type and kind of educational institution
That standard must take in special conditions for students with disabilities (art. 39)
Citizens have a right to free education in state institutions on general programmes
Parents pay a fee for a child's upbringing in preschool institutions, set by the Cabinet

sources.label: The Law of Turkmenistan on Education (new edition), art. 39 'Financing of educational activities' - Ministry of Education of Turkmenistan, National Information Center
Regulations on state preschool institutions - Ministry of Education of Turkmenistan, National Information Center

funding: The State assures a disabled person the medical and paramedical care they need (art. 18)
The CFPSESH is a public administrative establishment, created by décret 2014-142
Its 2021 subsidy split 92 percent to operations and 8 percent to equipment
Care is free for the destitute holding a disability card, in state medical institutions
A fund for the promotion of disabled persons is promised, its financing left to decree

funding: The Minister may establish government schools at which the Government provides special education
Education for school-age children in government schools is free and no fees may be charged
Disability may not bar a child from access to free primary and secondary education
The duty to support students with disabilities binds only within available resources

sources.label: Education Act 2011, Republic of Nauru, s. 73 free public education, s. 74 government schools, s. 95 provision for students with special educational needs

workforce: A logopedist is whoever their country of training licenses to practise (AB 2023 no. 36)

funding: Obras sociales owe disabled members full cover of the prestaciones basicas (Ley 24.901 a. 2)
Those with no obra social reach the same prestaciones through state bodies (Ley 24.901 art. 4)
Rehabilitation modules name fonoaudiologia among the types of attention (Res. 428/99)
Prestaciones de apoyo are capped at six hours a week (Res. 428/99, 2.3.1)
Cover for the uninsured comes from funds the national budget sets yearly (Ley 24.901 a. 7 e)

The MSP tarifario regulates the economic compensation traded between health subsystems (2014)
That tarifario prices terapia del lenguaje by the session (MSP tarifario 2014, code 291146)
Its listed values are a ceiling for payment between providers and funders, not a fixed fee

funding: Early intervention became one of the Ministry of Labour and Social Security's social programmes
It is the only fully publicly funded service for young children with disability
One private autism centre engaged a speech therapist on CHASE Fund money, 2008 to 2010
Speech therapy inside the programme is part time; physiotherapy is full time
The minister told Parliament in December 2023 that those therapies are free, at no cost
